director.summary: Moriarty Group delivered mixed performance across three stores this week with combined sales of €133.2k (+2.1% like-for-like) despite YTD sales declining €560k (-2.1%). Balbriggan surged 11.1% week-on-week with strong basket growth (+11.97%), while Palmerstown and Skerries showed modest gains. Waste reduction initiatives are working across all stores (-42.9% to -38.2% vs LY), but margin compression persists YTD across all three locations.

stores.name: Balbriggan

Margin slightly compressed (-0.50 pct) but absolute margin contribution solid at €6,484. Transaction count declining (-0.76%) suggests need for traffic building.

diagnosis.wrong: Moriarty Group is experiencing simultaneous margin compression (€183k YTD loss despite near-flat sales), transaction volume decline (-47,601 visits YTD at Palmerstown/Balbriggan), and acute waste deterioration at Skerries (+74.45% this week). YTD sales down €281k Palmerstown, €277k Balbriggan, partially offset by Skerries +€298k, masking deeper traffic loss.
diagnosis.why: Root causes appear to be: (1) aggressive promotional pricing eroding margins without corresponding volume recovery at Palmerstown/Balbriggan; (2) competitive pricing pressure on traffic-driver categories causing transaction count decline; (3) operational inconsistency at Skerries with weak waste controls despite largest format and resource base; (4) possible supply cost inflation not passed through pricing.
diagnosis.fix: Immediate actions: (A) halt margin-eroding promotions pending competitive audit; (B) deploy Palmerstown waste discipline playbook to Skerries within 48 hours; (C) execute Balbriggan basket-building strategy across all stores to recover €0.28 average spend; (D) commission margin recovery task force targeting +€50k by year-end through mix/pricing optimization, not volume gambles.
